message:
Working from photographs that have the dimensions marked is actually how I complete most of my projects, so yes, of course. I would also definitely be interested in long-term cooperation.
Best regards,
Nathaniel

Thank you for the offer. Based on the description, I could complete this first project for a fixed price of $950, with delivery estimated at 9–13 days. If that arrangement works for you, it would be my preference.
What do you think?

As some dimensions may require further clarification during the work, could you please remain available for questions and quick confirmation? I would also like you to confirm which steel grade should be used for the shaft and the other parts, and whether you have a company drawing template or any specific ČSN/EN ISO requirements.

Good evening, Mateo!
Are we moving ahead with the project? My availability next month is quite limited, so if we are proceeding, I would like to begin as soon as possible in order to meet the agreed timeline.
Please let me know.
Best regards,
Nathaniel
Sorry for replying late. For this first project in our cooperation, would a price range of 700USD be acceptable to you?

The only template I can provide is for Autodesk Inventor, although I am not sure whether that works for you. Otherwise, I have no additional preferences; the project simply needs to comply with the usual ČSN/EN standards.

Thank you for getting back to me, Mateo; no problem at all. I can accept $700 for the first project as the beginning of our cooperation.
Some dimensional or technical points may need clarification while I work. If questions come up, I will contact you so that we can resolve them quickly and keep the project progressing.
Provided everything goes well, I am confident there will be opportunities for us to collaborate on future projects too. Please send the fixed-price contract, and I will start immediately.
Because the part is currently in our storage, obtaining any measurements could slow my responses. Any resulting delay from my side is acceptable.

Thank you for the heads-up; that is no problem. Since some measurements may take time to obtain, I'll minimize interruptions by collecting my questions and sending them together whenever possible. I look forward to working with you.
This is the first time we've ever used this website, so we have very little experience with it. Sorry about that as well.
Everyone has to begin somewhere, Mateo, so there is no need to worry. I will make the process as smooth as I can, and you can contact me whenever you have questions about the platform.
The supplied template is from Inventor.
Our expected drawing setup is shown in this example.
Thanks in advance; please keep me informed about how the project is progressing.
Thank you, I understand. Within the next 10–12 hours, I’ll begin working on the project and will keep you informed of my progress.

Please take a look at this part and clarify its intended manufacturing method. Should it be a single solid piece, or should it consist of a separate ring with 10 welded lugs? The photo shows that it is welded to the flange, but it does not reveal whether the lugs are welded onto the ring or formed integrally with it.

The assembly has now been created, but progress is blocked by incomplete and conflicting information: some dimensions are absent, several others do not agree, and the installation locations for the 7 separate parts remain unclear.
I have compiled clarification questions and am awaiting your responses. Once I receive them, I will revise the model and send a sectional assembly view using the dimensions currently available. Additional corrections may still be necessary afterward.
I look forward to your feedback.

Thank you for the comments. Because I am travelling to customers, my response may be delayed, but I will try to answer everything clearly as soon as possible—next Thursday or no later than Friday. Would that timing be acceptable?
ok
Hello, I have now tried to address all of your notes. Hopefully the clarifications help, but if any information is still missing, please contact me. Thank you.

Understood, Mateo. Next Thursday, I will review all the information, complete the necessary revisions, and prepare a preliminary drawing for you to examine.
Best regards,
Nathaniel
What is the model of the sheet unwinder, please?

Could you clarify how the bushing assembly is actually put together? Several points remain unclear. I assume the 7 holes are for fastening it with screws, yet the dimensions suggest a very large interference fit: the bushing has an outer diameter of 84.6 mm, while the mating-part bore is 84 mm.
The countersinks appear designed to recess countersunk screw heads, but that would imply installation from the opposite side. This conflicts with the assumed arrangement.
In addition, the photographs omit some components from the complete shaft assembly. Consequently, the mechanism's operating principle is still not fully clear.

For confirmation of the final dimensions, I have added all measurements obtained so far to a preview drawing; this is not the final drawing. Please either remeasure the indicated dimensions or confirm them. In the preview, the shaft is depicted fully assembled and in its fully retracted position.
For faster communication, do you happen to use Telegram?
Could you clarify what you intended to communicate in that message?
Sorry, I don't have access.
After the maintenance team has reviewed it with us, we will let you know their feedback.
What is the unwinder's model, if it is commercially available?
It is custom-made solely for local purposes, so it is not really commercially available.

My understanding is the same. Before proceeding, I am waiting for you to verify the dimensions in the PDF I sent and explain the bushing arrangement. Its purpose is still not entirely clear; is it meant to function as a plain bearing?
Could you also provide any photographs of the complete machine that show how the shaft was installed?
Should I also send the 3D design package immediately?
Although I am unsure whether I can obtain photographs of the machine, the 3D design file would always be welcome.
Which file format would work best for you? I think the model is otherwise basically complete; as I noted earlier, the only part I still do not understand is how the bushing should be secured.
Ideally, please provide it as .ipt; at minimum, .stp would be acceptable. Thank you.
I will proceed for now with preparing the drawings for the individual parts. The bushing and dimensions will remain pending until I receive your feedback.
Do the drawings need to specify materials? If they do, for each part, which material should be identified?
Except for the bushing, please specify S355 JRG2 as the standard material for every part for now. The bushing should instead be CuSn12.
ок

Good evening, Mateo.
Attached is the first fully prepared drawing version. Please disregard the current bushing design because I still have not received details on how it should be installed and secured. For the moment, the drawing merely shows it held by 7 screws.
Good afternoon, Mateo. Do you have any corrections, comments, or additional requests at this stage, and is everything clear so far? Please also let me know when I should expect your feedback.
The review and clarification work is currently underway. Hopefully, I’ll get back to you next Wednesday with all the clarifications. Thanks for your patience.

Hello Nathaniel,
I have finally reviewed everything and checked your drawings. Please make the following changes:

1\. For POS 1+2+3, the required process differs from what I previously understood: the parts must first be premachined, then welded together, and finally machined.

2\. Use tube 168/36 as the raw material for the main shaft. Premachine it to establish the locations for POS 2+3.

3\. Place the previously unclear bushing inside the main shaft. **IMPORTANT**: my notes state this incorrectly—the bushing is not mounted to POS 4 and belongs only in the main shaft. Please select a suitable clearance between the shaft and bushing.

4\. POS 4 carries the piston/rod end and nut. The control-piston rod, which secures the sliding movement, runs inside the main shaft; therefore, the 82mm inner diameter must also be machined after welding.

5\. As indicated by cross section C-C on the main-shaft drawing, the keyway must be omitted. Make the M72x1.5 locking-nut thread wider, and increase the requested main-bushing space to 65mm.

6\. If possible, follow the numbering shown on the assembly when numbering the drawings.

Please let me know your progress, and thank you.

Although the bushing arrangement now looks logical, its length raises one more question. Compared with the machined seat inside the shaft, the bushing appears rather short; are you sure its length is correct?
The photos make the lugs appear offset, so I assumed that arrangement was intentional. Am I correct that they should instead be aligned in the same plane?

The drawings state it incorrectly. The bushing belongs inside the main shaft, and the control-piston rod is guided through that bushing. Therefore, you must choose a suitable clearance fit, such as H8/h9, between the bushing and the shaft's inner diameter. Only the piston end is located on the sliding part.
As shown in the picture and in your assembly, the axes of the holes should be separated by 120 degrees.
If the bushing is installed only inside the main shaft, are screws no longer needed to secure it? I think I’m getting confused again.
Would a clearance fit allow the bushing to sit loose and move around inside the shaft, or is it instead fitted rigidly onto the piston rod?

Since face 1 is already flat, I do not think it needs a machining allowance. After welding, keeping that face flat would not be possible if we machined it on a lathe. We could add the machining allowance to face 2 instead. Another option would be to leave an allowance on face 1 as well, then make it flat on a milling machine after welding. What do you think?

For now, please prepare it using this arrangement: secure the bushing in the sliding end with the rod nut, and have it slide inside the main shaft with its outside diameter serving as the contact surface. I had been told that the bushing sits only in the shaft, but this is the other possible solution I am considering. Once you finalize the drawings, I will present them to the maintanence manager, who may suggest a different idea.
Do we now keep the holes in both the bushing and the sliding mandrel, or should the holes in the bushing be removed?
Before they are welded onto the shaft, surfaces 1 and 2 must both be finalized. Neither surface should be machined afterward, because post-weld machining would be very bad. You’re right—is that okay?
Leave the holes in the bushing and sliding mandrel unchanged, please.
ок
Do you want me to remove the 9 mm groove?
That is a good question. Between the thread and the bearing surface, I think a small groove should remain, though perhaps it should be narrower.
I will prepare the fifth version and submit it for your approval either next Wednesday or early Thursday morning.
Excellent, many thanks.
Should it be 12.5 or 6.3?
Although there was some discussion about it, the final decision is 6,3. Please use 6,3 together with the given tolerance field.
Within 45 minutes, I will send V5. 👌
A set of drawings would be the best option, so there is no problem. I will review it next Tuesday.
The drawings are identical across the two files: one is in color, while the second uses the classic black-and-white presentation. I’ll wait for your feedback :)
Since I have some time available, I could handle additional work in parallel with the current project. Do you have any other projects at the moment? :)

Hi, and apologies for the delayed reply. I am away on a 9 days business trip, which has postponed my review, but I will probably check your drawings next Friday afternoon.
If I find everything satisfactory and have no additional comments, I will release the payment. Is that arrangement acceptable to you?
Also, if the production manager provides notes later, would you be willing to revise the drawings even after we have closed the project?
Additional projects do exist, but before we can look at them, I have to prepare everything for you.
From the quick look I can manage on my phone, it seems that the groove for the keyway is missing from the sliding mandrel part. As I wrote, I’ll review everything else later. Thank you.

Yes, Mateo, that arrangement is fine, and I will wait for your feedback. Please write to me whenever a correction is needed, including any later updates; I am available almost all the time. We will complete every required fix before finalizing everything.
I’ll add the keyway to the sliding mandrel—it is indeed missing there :)
To avoid saving the files several times, I’ll wait until all your comments arrive and then apply every correction together.

Good evening,
After reviewing the drawings, I find the version without colours easier to read. The 3D views may be coloured, but please keep every other view uncoloured.
Only very minor corrections remain; you can find them in the notes on the drawings.

Once we finalize the project, could you supply dwg/dxf files in addition to the pdf files?
For the models, will you provide only step files, or is there any possibility of receiving live, editable formats such as .ipt and .idw?

Thank you for making the updates.

Certainly, Mateo. I will export the drawings as DWG/DXF and provide the 3D models in STEP format. You will also receive the original editable SolidWorks files—SLDPRT, SLDASM and SLDDRW—for the parts, assemblies, and drawings. Beyond STEP, I can additionally export the models as SAT, IGES or IFC.

Because the overall dimension already gives the minimum and maximum values for the full travel, adding the indicated dimension would duplicate it. I need guidance before proceeding: should I retain the current overall dimension, or remove it and use the one you indicated instead?

The overall length is acceptable, but the functional dimension is the distance between those holes. Please add that dimension, and perhaps show the overall dimension in brackets.
First, send the final drawing set in pdf so that I can confirm it; only after that should you export the other formats.
The final deliverables should be PDF+DWG and STEP, together with native editable solidworks 3D part, assembly and drawing files.
ok

Hi,
The drawings in the final revision look quite good, so thank you. As I mentioned, would you be willing to implement any further small changes that arise, even after we close this project? You may also release all the files under our earlier agreement.
Thank you.

Of course—if any small adjustments are needed after this project closes, just message me and I will make them promptly. I am almost always available and also look forward to working with you on future projects.
Hopefully it reaches you soon; I’ve already released the payment.
I have corrected an issue I just found: 6 reference dimensions on the shaft blank had lost their associations.
For 3D models, these formats are standard.
